messages:
Mai: heads-up — spotted some routes showing negative marginal cost after cache/prefetch credits are applied. anyone else seeing negative unit cost in the console? :thinking:
Jordan: yep saw a dip on /chat/complete earlier. looks like prefetch warmups being credited twice for certain multi-hop chains.
Sam: i can repro. root cause seems to be attribution to the first-owner then a later refund when the cache hit materializes. quick repro i ran on staging:
```
curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/econ/sim -d '{"route":"/chat/complete","chain":["svc-A","svc-B"],"prefetch":true}'
```
Anika: UX: product teams are confused that "unit cost" goes negative. request: either hide negative adjusted numbers behind a toggle or show raw vs adjusted columns with clear help text.
Mai: proposal: add two side-by-side columns "raw token cost" and "adjusted (cache credits)". default to adjusted but show badge "why negative?" that expands to explanation. also: exclude canary traffic from amortized prefetch pools so experiments don't skew tenant economics.
Jordan: does this require an econ event schema change? right now prefetch credits are rolled into a single credit field, no lineage.
Sam: minimal opt-in schema additions: add optional strings route_chain_ids and owner_hint to econ.events when prefetch is applied. example flattened payload as a string in logs: '{route:/chat/complete,token_cost:12,cache_credit:-15,route_chain_ids:svc-A|svc-B,owner_hint:svc-A}'. these fields remain optional to limit cardinality.
Jordan: high-cardinality alert: route_chain_ids can explode storage. can we sample these tags? e.g., deterministic 5% sampling for standard tenants, full capture for canaries and paid tiers.
Mai: agree on deterministic sampling keyed by tenant-id (stable sample) so debugging is consistent. canary traffic gets 100% fidelity.
Anika: on the console side i'll add a toggle include/exclude cache credits and an inline tooltip with a 3-step animation showing amortization across prefetch windows. i'll need an econ API endpoint that returns both raw_series and adjusted_series (time series) for the selected route.
Sam: action list:
- Sam: add optional fields (route_chain_ids, owner_hint) + explicit cache_credit numeric to econ.event (opt-in).
- Sam/Jordan: implement deterministic sampling config and rollout (5% default, 100% canaries/ent).
- Anika: console toggle + help animation, UI mocks first.
- Mai: write RFC and update rollout docs to exclude canary from amortized pools.
Jordan: also propose an alert: fire if route 95p marginal cost < 0 for > 10m, to catch regressions.
Mai: yeah we should gate the alert behind a dry-run first. i'll draft an RFC tonight and add a checklist for the rollout (schema migr, sampling, UI flag, alert).
deploy-bot: econ-service v2.13.4 deployed to staging (hash:c1a2b3f)
Sam: tests green for schema change locally, opening PR for sampling config in ~20m.
Anika: i'll start a quick mock of the two-column table and post in #design for feedback.
Mai: thanks folks — short sync in 10 if anyone wants to pair on PRs. :thumbsup:
